IPC involves an active understanding of the circumstances, actions and consequences of the proposed act.

An individual who makes a reasoned choice to act after evaluating various alternative actions (or inaction) as well as the various possible consequences flowing from such action (or inaction), consents to such action.

After deliberating upon the various case laws, this Court summed up the legal position as under:
"To summarise the legal position that emerges -1- Cr. Revision No.318 of 2024 from the above cases, the "consent" of a woman with respect to Section 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.
To establish whether the "consent" was vitiated by a "misconception of fact" arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.
The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act."
In para - 24 of the said judgment, the factual matrix of the case has been discussed.

Para - 25 of the said judgment, reads as under :-
"25.
Considering the factual matrix of the case, parameters have been laid down and the Hon'ble Apex Court has discharged the applicant of that case.
5. In the present case, although the relationship between the parties was quite long but, it has been initiated on the false pretext of marriage.
There is a clear cut allegation that they were very good friend but finding the opportunity, as the victim was alone at her house, physical relationship was established.
Resistance has been overcome by giving false promise of marriage.
This is the specific allegation of the victim.
The further incident also suggests that there was a vitiated consent.
6. Every case has its own factual aspects.

Since in the present case the very initiation of sexual relationship was on vitiated consent rather on playing fraud with the victim, I find that the trial Ajit Kumar Mahato vs The State Of Jharkhand.
